execution_contract.why: the one route with next-open entry plus intrabar protective handling

execution_contract_native.why: the same contract on the native backend, for L07.1 fixed-intent parity

walkforward.why: the installed calendar WFO that arm A reproduces

walkforward_config.why: the config object whose modes LAB-04 traced; arm A must pin one of them

walkforward_support_matrix.why: declares which modes the install actually supports, instead of assuming five

candidate_selection.why: the installed selection rule arm A is labelled against

volatility_regime_labels.why: the registered M0 comparator (in-sample by construction, never an estimator)

engine_fill_trace_native.consequence: the rust backend exposes no per-fill trace, so Python/Rust parity is established on account path and orders, and full event-trace parity is never claimed
engine_fill_trace_native.lab_patch: handoff/lab_only_patch.diff would expose the fill vector; NOT applied

scheduler_callback.consequence: the installed engine has no refit-scheduler callback, so the lab drives the schedule from OUTSIDE the engine and feeds it fixed intents. The engine's economics are untouched, which is the point
scheduler_callback.lab_patch: none needed: driving from outside is the contract-preserving option

reroute_policy: an integration point that does not resolve is BLOCKED_CAPABILITY. It is never rerouted to a similar-looking symbol: a reroute succeeds, and a run that completes on economics the study did not register is worse than one that stops
lab_owns: when a parameter version becomes effective
